caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 605 of 2010.
lawyer:
Md Ali A kanda, Advocate instructed by Haridas Paul, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
Awlad Ali, Senior Advocate (with Mamunor Rashid, Advocate) instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Golzar Hossain (Md.) Advocate -----Petitioner
Vs.
Janata Bank ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
2. The back ground of this leave petition is that the petitioner filed the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division impugning the judgment and order dated 24-11-2008 passed by the learned District Judge, Sirajgonj in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 2008 affirming the order dated 29-7-2008 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Sirajgonj in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 2008. It further appears that there was apparent anomaly between the cause title and the prayer of the writ petition. In the cause title, the judgment and order dated 27-9-2009 passed by a learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.600 of 2009 was impugned, whereas in the prayer as stated hereinbefore the judgment and order of the learned District Judge passed in the Artha Rin miscellaneous appeal was impugned. However, from the Rule issuing order as noted in the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, it appears that the Rule was issued as per terms of the prayer made in the writ petition. 

 3. The case of the writ-petitioner as made out in the writ petition, in short, was that one Prodip Kumar Saha took loan of Taka 2 lac from Janata Bank, Ullapara Branch, Sirajgonj (hereinafter referred to as the Bank) on mortgaging 10 decimals of land. As Prodip Kumar Saha defaulted to repay the loan, the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No.147 of 1993 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sirajgonj against him for recovery of the loan amount with interest. The suit was decreed ex- parte for an amount of Taka 2,57,230.00 by the judgment and decree dated 20-10-1994. As the judgment-debtor failed to pay the decreetal amount, the Bank levied Artha Rin Execution Case No.49 of 1995. After the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain, 2003) had come into force, the said execution case was renumbered as Artha Execution Case No.235 of 2004 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Sirajgonj and in the execution case, notice was published for auction sale of the mortgaged property. The petitioner participated in the said auction on 21-1-2008, but failed to succeed. Thereafter, the petitioner as 3rd party claimant to a part of the auction sold property (hereinafter referred to as the property in question) filed an application under section 32 of the Ain, 2003, by depositing 25% of the decreetal amount as mandated in sub-section (2) of section 32 thereof (we do not consider it necessary to state the facts relating to the claim of the petitioner to the property in question in disposing of the leave petition). The application was registered as Artha Miscellaneous Case No. 01 of 2008. The Artha Rin Adalat by order dated 20-7- 2008 rejected the application. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order, the petitioner preferred Artha Miscellaneous Appeal No.03 of 2008 before the District Judge, Sirajgonj under section 41 of the Ain, 2003 by depositing 50% of the decreetal amount as mandated in sub-section (2) thereof. The appeal wasby the learned District Judge by his judgment and order dated 24-11-2008. Thereafter, the petitioner filed Civil Revision No.600 of 2009 before the High Court Division by depositing 75% of the decreetal amount presumably under section 42 of the Ain, 2003 read with section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code). The civil revision appeared for hearing before a Single Bench on 27-8-2009 as a top matter. When the revision was taken up for hearing the learned Judge of the Single Bench "pointed out that the case was misconceived instead of civil revision. Writ petitioner (sic) was to be filed and not Civil Revision." In view of the said observation of the learned Judge of the Single Bench, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that he had got instructions from his client not to proceed further with the Rule and accordingly, the Rule was discharged as "being not pressed." Then the petitioner filed the writ petition with the prayer as has been quoted hereinbefore. 

 5. The Rule was contested by the respondent, Janata Bank, by filing an affidavit-in-opposition supporting the order dated 28-7-2008 passed by the learned Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 2008 as well as the learned District Judge in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No.3 of 2008. 

 8. In the writ petition as well as in the leave petition, it has been specifically stated that against the judgment and order dated 24-11-2008 passed by the learned District Judge in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No.03 of 2008 affirming those of the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Rin miscellaneous case rejecting the application under section 32 of the Ain, 2003, the petitioner filed revision application before the High Court Division being Civil Revision No.600 of 2009, but the Rule of that civil revision had to be discharged by the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division as being not pressed on the submission made by the learned Advocate of the petitioner that he had instruction not to proceed further with the Rule in view of the observation of the learned Judge who heard the revision application that against the judgment and order passed in the said miscellaneous appeal a writ would lie and not revision. Then the petitioner filed the writ petition. 

 15. From the order passed in the civil revision, it further appears that in fact, the hearing of the revision application was concluded and 27-8-2009 was fixed for delivering judgment, so we find no reason to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that the Rule had to be discharged as being not pressed by the learned Advocate for the petitioner because of the observation of the learned Judge of the Single Bench who heard the Rule that against the judgment and order of the learned District Judge, writ would lie but not the revision, and then the petitioner filed the writ petition, but from the impugned judgment and order passed in the writ petition, it does not appear that the learned Judges, at all, considered the said statements made in the writ petition and applied their mind to the pertinent legal aspect as to whether the writ petition was at all maintainable. 

 16. In view of the above, we are left with no option but to decide first: whether against the judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge in the Artha Rin miscellaneous appeal, revision would lie or writ would lie. The Ain, 2003 is a Special Law and its provisions have to be adhered to very strictly. Chapter VII of the Ain, 2003 has dealt with the appeal and the revision. Section 40 of the Ain, 2003 has spoken about the applicability of the relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure in respect of appeal and revision to be filed under the said Ain Section 41 of the Ain has provided the procedure as to the filing and the disposal of an appeal against the decree or the order of an Artha Rin Adalat and section 42 thereof has dealt with the provision of revision. We consider it beneficial to quote above 3(three) sections of the Ain, 2003 for proper understanding whether the revision filed by the petitioner was maintainable or not, the said sections are as follows:- 

 17. From a reading of section 40 of the Ain, 2003, it is apparent that the provisions of appeal and revision of the Code such as sections 96, 104, Order XLI and section 115 respectively have been made applicable in respect of an appeal and a revision, if filed under the Ain, 2003 subject to the provisions of the said Ain, Here we are concerned with the revision, as there was no dispute about the miscellaneous appeal filed before the District Judge being Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No.03 of 2008 which was filed under section 41 of the Ain, 2003. 

 19. From the facts as stated hereinbefore, it is clear that the petitioner while filing the application under section 32 of the Ain, 2003 deposited 25% of the decreetal amount and then while filing the appeal before the District Judge under section 41 thereof deposited 50% of the decreetal amount and again after dismissal of the miscellaneous appeal filed the revision application before the High Court Division by depositing 75% of the decreetal amount. Thus, there was no procedural defect or loopholes in filing the revision application by the petitioner and admittedly the Rule was not discharged on any procedural defect in filing the revision application, but as being not pressed on the observation of the learned Judge of the Single Bench that the revision application was not maintainable, instead filing of the writ petition was the proper forum. 

 20. From the above, it is also clear that the petitioner was vigilant very much in pursuing his claim to the property in question and he took right step in filing the revision application before the High Court Division and the revision was really maintainable, but unfortunately the Rule in the civil revision was discharged as being not pressed on the observation made by the learned Judge of the Single Bench. In this regard, it is to be noted that from the order passed in the revision discharging the Rule as being not pressed, it appears that the very learned Advocate who appeared on behalf of the Bank in the writ petition also appeared before the revisional Court while the Rule was discharged as being not pressed. In the affidavit-in-opposition filed in the writ petition, the facts asserted in the writ petition that while hearing the revision application, the learned Judge of the Single Bench observed that the revision application was not maintainable and instead the petitioner ought to have filed a writ petition and on such observation the learned Advocate for the petitioner got the Rule discharged as being not pressed have not been denied. Therefore, we find nothing wrong on the part of the petitioner to pursue his remedy in a proper forum, and we are constrained to say that the revisional Court without caring to see the law, namely, sections 40 and 42 of the Ain, 2003 observed that the revision application filed by the petitioner against the judgment passed in the Artha Rin miscellaneous appeal was not maintainable. The learned Judges of the Division Bench also while disposing of the writ petition totally failed to consider the above mentioned provisions of the Ain, 2003. In the context, we feel it necessary to reiterate the statement of law that when there is an alternative forum provided by a Statute, here the Ain, 2003, the power of Judicial review under article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh can not be invoked unless it can be shown that the alternative remedy is not efficacious or adequate, the wrong complained of is inextricably mixed up and the vires of the Statute or a statutory provision is challenged. We hold that in the facts and circumstances of the instant case, the revisional forum as provided in section 42 of the Ain, 2003 was definitely efficacious and the petitioner rightly filed the revision application being Civil Revision No.600 of 2009 before the High Court Division, but the Rule had to be discharged on the wrong observation made by the learned Judge of the Single Bench. We further observe that before entering into the merit of a writ petition the judges owe a duty to see whether the writ petition is maintainable in law, and in the case in hand since the writ petition was not maintainable the learned Judges ought not to have entered into the merit of the petitioner's claim to the property in question. 

 21. Be that as it may, since the petitioner filed the writ petition under misconception of law on the observation made by the learned Judge of the Single Bench as stated hereinbefore, he cannot be subjected to suffering for no fault of his own and the revision application filed by him deserve to be disposed of on merit. Therefore, whatever findings have been given by the learned Judges of the High Court Division in the impugned judgment and order as to the merit of the claim of the petitioner to the property in question cannot stand. Accordingly, the findings given by the High Court Division in the impugned judgment and order about the merit of the claim of the petitioner to the property in question are expunged. If so advised, the petitioner may take appropriate step for revival/restoration of the Rule to its file and number issued in the Civil Revision being No.600 of 2009 which was discharged as being not pressed on 27-8-2009 for disposal on merit in the light of the observations and the findings given hereinbefore.
